q: Which way do you read Arabic?
why: Arabic runs from right to left; the first letter of a word is the one on the right.

q: What tells ب, ت and ث apart?
o: Where they sit in the word
why: They share one shape: one dot below is ب, two above is ت, three above is ث.

q: What does ة at the end of سَيَّارَة tell you?
why: ة (taa marbuta) is the usual feminine ending, said -a.

q: Which letter is the breathy h from the throat?
why: ح is the breathy throat h; ه is the plain English h.

q: In the romanisation, what does a dot under a letter (ṣ, ṭ) mean?
why: ṣ ḍ ṭ ẓ are the heavy letters and ḥ is the throat h: the dot marks the sound English doesn't have.

q: What happens if you say قَلْب 'heart' with an English k?
o: Nothing: q and k are the same
why: q and k are different letters: قَلْب is 'heart', كَلْب is 'dog'.

q: What does the line over ā in the romanisation mean?
o: The vowel is long: hold it
why: The line marks a long vowel: ā ī ū are held about twice as long as a i u.

q: Which mark is kasra, the short i?
o: A little و above the letter
A small circle above the letter
why: Kasra sits below the letter, as in بِنْت.

q: How is a long ū written?
why: Damma + و gives the long ū, as in بُو.

q: Which letter never joins to the letter after it?
why: ر is one of the six non-joining letters: ا د ذ ر ز و.

q: What is لا?
o: A sign for a long vowel
ل followed by ا, joined in one shape
why: لا is lām + alif written as one shape, as in لَا, 'no'.

q: Why is there a gap inside سَيَّارَة?
o: ا and ر never join to the next letter
why: Non-joining letters leave a gap inside the word; سَيَّارَة is still one word.

q: What does sukun tell you?
o: Hold the letter twice as long
why: Sukun is the small circle: the letter has no vowel, as in مَكْتَب.

q: What does shadda do?
why: Shadda doubles the letter: مُدَرِّسَة has a held r.

q: In بَيْت, what do fatha + ي with sukun sound like?
o: ay, close to the i in 'bite'
why: Fatha + ي with sukun is the gliding vowel ay.

q: How is ى at the end of عَلَى said?
why: ى, the alif maqsura, is a long ā, as in عَلَى.

q: What does tanwin -an need in the spelling?
o: An extra ا after the letter
why: The doubled fatha comes with an extra ا: شُكْرًا.

q: What does hamza sit on at the start of أَنَا?
why: At the start of a word hamza sits on ا: أ above or إ below.

q: What happens to the ل of ال before a sun letter such as ش?
o: It is not said; the sun letter is doubled
why: Sun letters swallow the l: الشَّمْس, with shadda on ش.

q: What does الْبَيْت كَبِير mean?
o: the house of the big one
why: No article on كَبِير makes it a sentence: no 'is' needed.

q: How do you say 'the big house'?
why: Both words take the article, and the describing word comes second.

q: Someone says السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُم. What's the reply?
why: The reply turns the greeting around: وَعَلَيْكُم السَّلَام, 'and upon you peace'.

q: Why does صَبَاح have no ال in صَبَاح الْخَيْر?
o: Words for times of day never take ال
It is the first word of an iḍāfa, which never takes the article
ال is only for feminine words
why: In an iḍāfa ('morning of the good') only the second word takes the article.

q: How do you ask a woman how she is?
why: To a woman the ending has kasra: حَالُكِ.

q: Which word is feminine?
why: سَيَّارَة ends in ة, the feminine sign.

q: Why is أُمّ feminine?
why: A few words are feminine by meaning, with no ة: أُمّ, بِنْت, أُخْت.

q: You're talking about a car (سَيَّارَة). 'It' is:
why: سَيَّارَة is feminine, so 'it' is هِيَ.

q: Which word is 'you' to a woman?
why: To a woman: أَنْتِ, with kasra under the ت.

q: A man says 'I'm a student.' Which is right?
why: A man speaking: the masculine طَالِب agrees with him.

q: What is 'it' for a book (كِتَاب)?
why: كِتَاب is masculine, so 'it' is هُوَ.

q: How do you say "The house is big"?
why: Subject and predicate side by side, with no word for "is" and no article on كَبِير.

q: What does الْبَيْت الْكَبِير mean?
why: With the article on both words it is a phrase, "the big house", not a sentence.

q: A woman wants to say "I'm busy". Which is right?
why: No "am" in Arabic, and the adjective agrees with the woman speaking: مَشْغُولَة.

q: How do you say "a car"?
why: Arabic has no word for "a": سَيَّارَة on its own means "a car".

q: Which one means "the new apartment"?
why: A phrase puts the article on both words, and the adjective agrees with the feminine شَقَّة.

q: Why does أُحِبّ الْقَهْوَة (I like coffee) have ال?
o: Coffee in general takes the article
Every noun after أُحِبّ needs ال, even names
It can only mean one particular cup
why: Arabic uses the article for things in general, where English uses nothing.

q: How does a woman say "I'm Egyptian"?
why: A woman uses the feminine nisba, with ة: مِصْرِيَّة.

q: The country is الْمَغْرِب. How do you say "He's Moroccan"?
why: The nisba drops the article of الْمَغْرِب and adds -ī.

q: What does الْعَرَبِيَّة mean on its own?
why: A language is the feminine nisba with the article.

q: Which word asks "what" before a noun, as in "What's your name?"
why: مَا goes before a noun or pronoun; مَاذَا goes before a verb.

q: How do you turn الْبَيْت كَبِير into a yes / no question?
o: Put هَل in front: هَل الْبَيْت كَبِير؟
Put مَا in front: مَا الْبَيْت كَبِير؟
why: هَل goes in front and nothing else changes.

q: "Where's the school?" =
why: أَيْنَ means where; it comes first, and there is no word for "is".

q: How do you read ٤٧?
why: Digits run left to right even in Arabic text: ٤ then ٧ is 47.

q: How do you say "twenty-one"?
why: Units first, then وَ and the tens: "one and twenty".

q: "one school" =
why: "One" comes after the noun and agrees with the feminine مَدْرَسَة: وَاحِدَة.

q: How do you say "please" to a waitress?
why: To a woman: مِن فَضْلِكِ, with a kasra under the ك.

q: Why is it بِكَم هٰذِهِ؟ when you point at a bag (حَقِيبَة)?
o: بِكَم always takes هٰذِهِ after it
why: "This" agrees with the thing: حَقِيبَة ends in ة, so هٰذِهِ.

q: What does الْحِسَاب مِن فَضْلِكَ mean?
why: الْحِسَاب is the check; مِن فَضْلِكَ is please, to a man.

q: Where does the adjective go?
o: Before the noun, with ال: الْكَبِير بَيْت
why: Arabic adjectives follow the noun.

q: "the new car" =
why: Both words take the article, and the adjective agrees with the feminine سَيَّارَة.

q: What does الْبَيْت الْكَبِير جَمِيل mean?
o: The house is big and beautiful.
why: الْبَيْت الْكَبِير is the subject (both words have ال); جَمِيل, with no ال, is the predicate.

q: "the student's book" =
why: The owned thing comes first, with no article; the owner second, with the article.

q: Which word of an iḍāfa never takes ال?
why: The ال (or a name) on the second word makes the whole phrase definite.

q: In جَامِعَةْ تُولْسَا, how is the end of جَامِعَة said?
why: A ة at the end of the first word of an iḍāfa is said -at.

q: "my house" =
why: بَيْتِي means "my house", and the ending already makes it definite: no ال.

q: What happens to the ة of مَدِينَة before "my"?
why: Before a possessive ending, ة is written as an ordinary ت.

q: Which one means "your name" when you talk to a woman?
why: To a woman: اِسْمُكِ, with a kasra. اِسْمُكَ is to a man, اِسْمُهَا is "her name", اِسْمِي is "my name".

q: How does Arabic usually say "I have"?
why: Arabic has no verb "have": عِنْدِي, literally "with me".

q: Which sentence means "I don't have a car"?
why: عِنْدِي is not a verb, so it takes لَيْسَ, not لَا, and لَيْسَ comes first.

q: What does عِنْدَهَا mean?
why: عِنْدَهَا ends in the possessive ending for "her": she has.

q: What is the plural of كِتَاب (book)?
why: كِتَاب has a broken plural: the inside changes, كُتُب.

q: How do you say "The cars are new"?
why: A plural of things takes a feminine singular adjective, with no article on the predicate.

q: What does مُدَرِّسَات mean?
why: The ending -āt makes the feminine plural: a group of women teachers.

q: What do كِتَاب, كَاتِب and مَكْتَب have in common?
o: The root letters ك ت ب
why: All three are built on the root ك ت ب, "writing".

q: What does the shape of مَكْتَب and مَطْعَم usually make?
why: The ma- pattern often names a place: the place of writing, the place of eating.

q: Which word shares a root with مُدَرِّس (teacher)?
why: مُدَرِّس and مَدْرَسَة both carry the root د ر س, "study".

q: Which word means "I study"?
why: The prefix أَ says "I": أَدْرُس.

q: How do you say "You study" to a woman?
why: To a woman: أَنْتِ, and the verb adds -īn: تَدْرُسِين.

q: Is أَدْرُس الْعَرَبِيَّة a complete sentence without أَنَا?
o: No: Arabic always needs the pronoun
Only when a woman is speaking
why: The prefix shows who, so the pronoun is often left out.

q: What is تَدْرُس سَارَة الْعَرَبِيَّة?
o: a question: Does Sara study Arabic?
a normal statement: Sara studies Arabic.
a mistake: the name must come first
why: Verb first is an ordinary statement in Arabic; questions use هَل.

q: When the verb comes first, before a plural subject like الطُّلَّاب, the verb is…
why: Before its subject the verb stays singular: يَعْمَل الطُّلَّاب.

q: Sara is a woman. Which verb goes with her, before or after her name?
why: A woman takes the same form as هِيَ: تَدْرُس, in either order.

q: Which word means "not" in front of a present verb like أَعْرِف?
why: Present verbs take لَا: لَا أَعْرِف.

q: How do you say "I don't have a car"?
why: عِنْدِي is not a verb, so it takes لَيْسَ.

q: How do you say "She isn't here"?
why: No verb, so لَيْسَ, and it agrees with هِيَ: لَيْسَت.

q: Where does جِدًّا (very) go?
o: at the start of the sentence
after the noun, before the adjective
why: جِدًّا follows the adjective: كَبِير جِدًّا.

q: Which means "every day"?
why: كُلّ يَوْم has no article; كُلّ الْيَوْم means "all day" and الْيَوْم is "today".

q: Which means "Monday"?
why: A day is an iḍāfa: يَوْم with no article, then the day word with the article.

q: Which word means "I studied"?
why: The ending -tu says "I": دَرَسْتُ.

q: Fatima went to the market. Which verb?
why: Fatima is a woman, and it is the past: the ending -at, ذَهَبَت.

q: What does دَرَسْنَا mean?
why: The ending -nā says "we"; there is no prefix, so it is the past.

q: How do you say "excuse me" to a woman?
why: To a woman the last vowel is i: لَوْ سَمَحْتِ.

q: Which means "the train station"?
why: Iḍāfa: no article on the first word, the article on the second.

q: Which means "on the right"?
why: الْيَمِين is the right; الْيَسَار is the left.
